## In one sentence

Optimisation chooses inputs that minimise a loss or maximise an objective under
specified constraints.

## Local search

For a differentiable function, an interior stationary point satisfies
$\nabla f=0$. In one dimension, the second derivative helps classify a point:
positive curvature suggests a local minimum and negative curvature a local
maximum.

Gradient descent updates parameters in the direction of decreasing loss:

$$
\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t+1} = \boldsymbol{\theta}_t - \eta \nabla L(\boldsymbol{\theta}_t)
$$

The learning rate $\eta$ controls the step size.

## Constraints and global structure

A local optimum need not be the best point globally. Constraints can change the
answer and may require methods such as Lagrange multipliers. Convex problems
are especially useful because every local minimum is global under suitable
conditions.

::: {.callout-tip}
An optimisation result is only as meaningful as its objective, constraints,
and scale. Always state what is being optimised and what trade-off it encodes.
:::

## Check your understanding

For a one-variable loss, sketch how changing the learning rate affects the path
taken by gradient descent.
